Registration data only — for DNS/mail health as well, use domain_health_check; for a combined report, use domain_report.

tools.name: domain_availability_check
tools.description: Check whether a domain is registered, plus scan common typo-squat variants (adjacent-key substitution, letter omission/doubling, transposition) across popular TLDs (.com, .net, .org, .io, .co, .ai, .app, .dev) for brand-protection or domain-flipping research. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: url_to_markdown, security_headers_audit, redirect_chain_check, page_performance_check, structured_data_extract, tech_stack_fingerprint, seo_audit, broken_link_check, email_deliverability_check, safe_browsing_check, ssl_labs_grade, pagespeed_insights, github_repo_health_check, email_address_validate, smtp_server_check · Private data: security_headers_audit, ai_readiness_audit, domain_health_check, dns_propagation_check, email_deliverability_check, whois_lookup, check_open_ports, safe_browsing_check, exposed_files_check, pagespeed_insights, package_vulnerability_check, email_address_validate, smtp_server_check · Public sink: email_deliverability_check, email_address_validate · Destructive: seo_audit, ai_readiness_audit, pagespeed_insights.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
